title: Transferring a Vehicle Service Contract to a Private Buyer
content:
Training notes on the transfer rule of Vehicle Service Contracts.

**The rule.** A service contract may be transferred only while it is active, only after the retail installment contract financing the vehicle is paid off, and only to a private buyer of the vehicle, on a request made within the plan's transfer window after the private sale, for the plan's transfer fee paid by the borrower. A transfer keeps the original expiration date, expiration odometer, claims history and lifetime limit.

**Questions answered by the rule**

*Which service contracts can be transferred?* Only one whose status is active. A cancelled or expired Vehicle Service Contract is not transferred.

*Can a service contract be transferred while the vehicle is still financed?* No. A transfer is made only after the retail installment contract financing the vehicle is paid off.

*Who may receive the transfer?* Only a private buyer of the vehicle.

*When must the transfer be requested?* Within the plan's transfer window, counted after the private sale of the vehicle.

*Who pays the transfer fee?* The borrower.

*Does the new owner get a fresh term or a fresh limit?* No. The transferred contract keeps its original expiration date and expiration odometer, its claims history and its lifetime limit.

**What the transfer record shows.** The new owner's name as on the bill of sale, and the date the transfer was recorded.

**Hypothetical case.** A borrower pays off a retail installment contract, sells the vehicle privately and asks for the active DriveSure Gold service contract to be transferred to the buyer within the transfer window. The transfer meets each condition; the buyer receives the contract with the same expiration date and odometer and the same claims history and lifetime limit, the borrower paying the transfer fee.
